$comment: Machine-readable audit rules. Identifiers here must appear in skills/anti-ai-design/references/anti-patterns.md (enforced by npm run validate). codeSignals are heuristic hints for locating candidates in markup; a hit is never a verdict, and visual judgment requires a capable model and, when possible, rendered evidence.

severityLevels.definition: Blocks a core task or creates a serious accessibility or functional problem.
Materially damages usability, hierarchy, or visual coherence.
Weakens quality or consistency but does not block the primary task.
A minor refinement or optional enhancement.

evidenceTypes.definition: Directly seen in the provided screenshot, rendered interface, design file, or code.
Deduced from partial evidence (e.g. a static screenshot implies but cannot prove missing focus states).
The available evidence cannot answer the question; state what evidence would.

rules.title: Automatic badge + headline + description stack
evidence: Eyebrow/pill/label above a large headline, followed by a short paragraph and optional CTA
The same stack opens most sections
Eyebrow restates the headline
legitimateWhen: The label carries real navigational, status, date, or step information
Used once, deliberately, where the hierarchy serves the content
alternatives: Standalone specific headline
Heading embedded in a demonstration or diagram
Statement without supporting paragraph
Compact heading followed directly by content
Side-column heading beside long content

rules.title: Repetitive equal-weight feature card grid
evidence: 3-8 uniform cards with icon, title, one-sentence description
Items of unequal importance given equal weight
Generic icons
Removing a card would go unnoticed
legitimateWhen: Items are independent entities the user browses, compares, or selects
Each card controls or links to something distinct
Cards carry real, differing data
The set is user- or data-driven (catalog, templates, plans, widgets)
alternatives: Rank and demonstrate the top one or two; list the rest
Timeline for processes
Table for comparison
Annotated screenshot for aspects of one workflow
One strong proof point instead of many weak claims

rules.title: Island mode / over-containerization
evidence: Most content in floating rounded rectangles with own background, border, shadow
Containers nested two or more levels
Header, sidebar, and content each a separate floating island
legitimateWhen: Overlays, popovers, dialogs
Draggable or selectable objects
Regions with independent scroll
Widgets with their own data and controls (one level)
alternatives: Remove outer containers; let alignment and background define regions
Group with spacing
Single divider or background shift between regions
Rows and columns for dense data

rules.title: Borders and shadows on everything
evidence: Most elements carry both border and shadow
Separators duplicate spacing
Shadows on static in-page content
legitimateWhen: Form field edges
Focus rings
Table structure aiding scanning
Overlays above content
Items being dragged
Selected state
alternatives: One separation device per hierarchy level
Delete all, re-add only where absence causes a real problem

rules.title: Default generic gradients
evidence: Purple-to-blue or pink-to-orange gradients on hero, headline text, buttons
Blurred color blobs behind content
Gradient unrelated to brand
legitimateWhen: Gradient belongs to the established brand
Gradient encodes information (scale, time, material)
Text contrast verified across the gradient
alternatives: Color derived from brand and content
Flat confident color field
Typography or imagery as the anchor

rules.title: Excessive radii and pill shapes
evidence: Large radii on tables, images, full-width sections
Every button and tag is a pill
Nested elements share outer radius
legitimateWhen: Brand is genuinely soft or playful
Platform conventions
Pill shape consistently marks one component type
alternatives: Small radius scale tied to size and role
Nested radius = outer minus padding
Square edges for document-like content

rules.title: Repeated symmetrical section layouts
evidence: Every section centered and symmetrical
Mechanical image-left/text-right alternation
legitimateWhen: Content is genuinely parallel and consistency aids comparison
alternatives: Structure per section from content
Vary scale, width, density by importance
Asymmetry where one element should dominate

rules.title: Generic SaaS visual identity
evidence: Dark navy/black with one neon accent
Same sans at same weights everywhere
Glowing borders, abstract 3D shapes
Interchangeable 'platform for modern teams' copy
legitimateWhen: Never as a default bundle; dark UI alone can be justified by context
alternatives: Art direction from product intent
Type with roles
Color from the domain
Show the actual product

rules.title: Arbitrary decorative elements
evidence: Floating circles, dot grids, sparkles, orbs unrelated to content
legitimateWhen: Part of a defined illustration or brand system with purpose
alternatives: Use content as the visual: product UI, data, photography, diagrams

rules.title: Sections without content-driven reason
evidence: Stock landing-page sequence regardless of product
Placeholder logo strip
Repeated CTA bands
legitimateWhen: Each section answers a real visitor question with real material
alternatives: One section per real visitor question, in order
Drop sections without material

rules.title: Emoji as production iconography
evidence: Emoji used as feature, navigation, or status icons
legitimateWhen: User-generated content, reactions, chat, or an intentionally informal voice with accessible markup
alternatives: Consistent icon set or platform symbols
No icon

rules.title: Decorative glassmorphism
evidence: Frosted translucent panels for ordinary content over blurred gradients
legitimateWhen: Platform material semantics for layers above content, respecting reduce-transparency settings
alternatives: Solid surfaces with verified contrast
Translucency only for floating layers

rules.title: Placeholder or fabricated content presented as real
evidence: Invented metrics, testimonials, or logos
Lorem ipsum in shipped UI
Sample data indistinguishable from production
legitimateWhen: Never presented as real; clearly marked placeholders during design are fine
alternatives: Request real content
Bracketed placeholders
Realistic lengths including long and empty cases

rules.title: Micro-labels and pills everywhere
evidence: Decorative uppercase tags and badges on most elements
legitimateWhen: Labels encode state or classification the user acts on
alternatives: Remove decision-free labels
Express category through grouping

rules.title: Gratuitous motion
evidence: Every section animates on scroll
Hover effects on non-interactive elements
Looping decorative animation
legitimateWhen: Motion explains change, gives feedback, or is the product; reduced motion respected
alternatives: Remove by default; add motion with a stated job

rules.title: Unclear focal point
evidence: Several elements compete at the same visual weight
Reviewer cannot name the first thing to look at
legitimateWhen: Deliberately neutral views such as data grids where the user chooses focus
alternatives: One dominant element per view, sized and positioned for the primary task

rules.title: Weak typographic hierarchy
evidence: Levels differ by size only slightly
Too many sizes or weights
Headings not distinguishable from body
legitimateWhen: Dense tools using weight and position over size, consistently
alternatives: Fewer levels with clearer contrast
Defined type roles

rules.title: Poor spacing rhythm
evidence: Arbitrary gaps
Related items as far apart as unrelated ones
legitimateWhen: Intentional break in rhythm marking a transition
alternatives: Spacing scale tied to relationship strength

rules.title: Inconsistent alignment
evidence: Edges that almost align
Mixed centered and left-aligned text without reason
legitimateWhen: Deliberate offset used as a compositional device, clearly not accidental
alternatives: Shared alignment lines from a grid

rules.title: Inappropriate density
evidence: Expert tools padded so users must scroll for basic information
Consumer flows crammed
legitimateWhen: Density matched to frequency of use and expertise
alternatives: Density modes
Progressive disclosure
Compact tables for operators

rules.title: Excessive decoration
evidence: Ornament competes with content for attention
legitimateWhen: Expressive brand contexts where decoration is the message and content remains legible
alternatives: Remove ornament and let content carry identity

rules.title: Lack of compositional intent
evidence: Elements stacked in source order with uniform treatment
No relationship between text and imagery
legitimateWhen: Simple documents where linear order is the intent
alternatives: Compose from content priority; define relationships between elements

rules.title: Primary and secondary actions not distinguished
evidence: Multiple equally prominent buttons
Destructive action styled as primary without safeguard
legitimateWhen: Genuinely equal choices (e.g. two balanced options) presented neutrally
alternatives: One primary per view; secondary and tertiary styles

rules.title: Unclear navigation
evidence: Current location not indicated
Inconsistent navigation between screens
legitimateWhen: Single-screen tools without navigation
alternatives: Persistent, platform-appropriate navigation with current state

rules.title: Ambiguous labels
evidence: Generic 'Submit', 'Learn more', icon-only buttons without labels
legitimateWhen: Universally understood icons with accessible names
alternatives: Verb + object labels

rules.title: Weak interaction feedback
evidence: No pressed, pending, or completed feedback
legitimateWhen: Instant actions whose result is visible immediately
alternatives: State change on press, progress for waits, confirmation on completion

rules.title: Poor error prevention and recovery
evidence: Errors without explanation or path forward
Destructive actions without undo or confirmation
Form loses input on error
alternatives: Inline specific messages, preserved input, undo

rules.title: Missing empty states
evidence: Blank area or broken layout when no data
alternatives: Explain why empty and the next action

rules.title: Inadequate keyboard interaction
evidence: Common actions require pointer
No shortcuts in expert tools
alternatives: Full keyboard operability; shortcuts for frequent actions

rules.title: Confusing information architecture
evidence: Grouping does not match user mental model
Same item reachable under conflicting labels
alternatives: Group by user task; test labels against user vocabulary

rules.title: Insufficient contrast
evidence: Text below 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text)
UI component boundaries below 3:1
legitimateWhen: Disabled controls and incidental text are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3
alternatives: Adjust tokens; verify with a contrast checker

rules.title: Missing or invisible focus indicators
evidence: outline: none without replacement
Focus hidden behind sticky elements
alternatives: Visible :focus-visible styles with sufficient contrast

rules.title: Inaccessible custom controls
evidence: div or span with click handler and no role, tabindex, or key handling
alternatives: Native elements; otherwise follow ARIA Authoring Practices

rules.title: Poor reading or focus order
evidence: Visual order differs from DOM order
Positive tabindex values
alternatives: Source order matches reading order; avoid positive tabindex

rules.title: Inadequate text scaling
evidence: Fixed pixel heights clip text at 200%
Ignores Dynamic Type or font scale
alternatives: Relative units, flexible containers, platform text styles

rules.title: Missing accessible names
evidence: Icon-only buttons without labels
Inputs without associated labels
Images without alt
legitimateWhen: Decorative images with empty alt
alternatives: Visible labels; aria-label only when a visible label is impossible

rules.title: Unnecessary motion without reduced-motion support
evidence: Large-scale motion with no prefers-reduced-motion handling
Auto-playing motion over 5 seconds without pause
legitimateWhen: Essential motion with alternatives
alternatives: Respect reduced-motion; provide pause controls

rules.title: Inadequate touch or pointer targets
evidence: Targets below platform minimums (WCAG 24x24 CSS px AA; Apple 44x44 pt default on iOS; Android 48x48 dp)
legitimateWhen: Inline text links and targets meeting WCAG spacing exceptions
alternatives: Enlarge hit area with padding, not only the visual

rules.title: Broken layout
evidence: Overlapping or clipped elements at supported sizes
alternatives: Intrinsic layout (flex/grid) and testing at real breakpoints

rules.title: Overflow and long-content failure
evidence: Long names, translations, or numbers break layout
Horizontal page scroll at 320 CSS px
legitimateWhen: Data tables with deliberate horizontal scroll inside their own region
alternatives: min-width: 0, wrapping, truncation with full value available

rules.title: Inconsistent responsive behavior
evidence: Components adapt differently without reason
Desktop layout merely shrunk
alternatives: Defined adaptation strategy per component

rules.title: Duplicated styles and magic numbers
evidence: Same values hard-coded across components
One-off overrides
legitimateWhen: Documented one-off exceptions
alternatives: Tokens and shared components

rules.title: Incorrect component semantics
evidence: Links used as buttons or vice versa
Headings chosen for size
Tables built from divs
alternatives: Semantic elements matching behavior

rules.title: Unnecessary dependencies
evidence: Libraries added for decorative effects
Second UI framework added alongside the existing one
legitimateWhen: Dependency solves a real, hard problem the stack lacks
alternatives: Platform features and existing dependencies

rules.title: Runtime errors
evidence: Console errors, crashes, failed builds where tooling exists to check
alternatives: Fix root cause; rerun checks

rules.title: Missing interaction states
evidence: No hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, or empty states where relevant
legitimateWhen: States genuinely not applicable to the component
alternatives: State matrix per component

anchors.1: Present but weak; multiple significant problems
anchors.4: Excellent; no meaningful problems found with the evidence available

gates.when: any open finding with severity critical
any open finding with severity high in category D
fewer than half of total weight assessable
